title: Adaptive rollback calibrator with cohort-aware baselining
creator: Ravi Sharma
description: Design and implement an adaptive rollback calibration service that computes and tunes rollback thresholds per deployment cohort. Current fixed-threshold rollbacks create false positives for latency-sensitive but low-error workloads, and miss regressions in high-throughput customers. This work builds a cohort-aware baselining + statistical decision layer that produces conservative, explainable rollback triggers for multi-metric SLOs (latency p95/p99, error rate, token-cost-per-request, throughput) and integrates with the existing rollout controller and canary pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Calibrator service returns per-cohort threshold recommendations and a confidence score for each metric
Rollout controller can consume calibrator signals and enact automated rollback when probability of SLO breach > 0.95 over configured lookback
Simulated shadow traffic tests show reduction in false-positive rollbacks by >= 40% versus baseline fixed thresholds on historical traffic
Dashboards showing cohort baselines, posterior distributions, and active rollouts are available in Console (runtime-1.19 release)
Documentation and runbook for incidents and manual override completed
implementation_notes: Components: metric-aggregator (stream daily aggregates), baseline-db (time-series per cohort), calibrator (Bayesian posterior calculator + sequential test engine), decision-api (REST hook consumed by rollout-controller)
Cohort keys: customer-id, route, model-variant, region; initial cohorting rule: top-75% traffic by route + region + model; fallback to global baseline for low-volume cohorts

Statistical approach: use conjugate priors for error-rate (beta-binomial), log-normal baseline for latency; sequential probability ratio test (SPRT) for fast detection with configurable type-I/II error bounds; support bootstrap CI for token-cost metric
Safety nets: minimum sample size per cohort (configurable), exponential backoff on repeated rollbacks, sticky suppression window (cooldown) after manual override
Integration: decision-api returns JSON: {signal, metric, posterior_p, suggested_threshold, reason}; rollout-controller already expects similar schema — adapt with compatibility shim
Performance: calibrator must handle 2k cohorts with 1min recompute cadence; use approximate aggregation for tail latency (t-digest summaries) to avoid heavy storage
test_plan: Unit tests for posterior calculators and SPRT logic
Synthetic replay using 90 days of anonymized request traces: compare fixed-threshold policy vs calibrator across metrics
Shadow deploy calibrator for 2 weeks: log decisions without enforcing them, compute ROC-style evaluation and suggested thresholds
Canary A/B: route 1% traffic to calibrator-driven rollout-controller and 1% to baseline for 4 rollouts; measure false-positive rollback rate and detection latency
Chaos tests: inject latency spikes, token-cost regressions, and simultaneous throughput drops to verify multi-signal harmonization
Postmortem drills: run simulated incident and verify runbook for manual cutoff and reasoned rollback explanations
